:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{9}{|9 x|\sqrt{(9 x)^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Use the linear substitution $u=9 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=9,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{9})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

The substitution factor is positive, so the absolute values satisfy

$$
|u|=|9 x|=9|x|,\qquad \frac{1}{|x|}=\frac{9}{|u|}.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsec}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{9}{|9 x|\sqrt{(9 x)^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 9\int \frac{1}{|9 x|\sqrt{(9 x)^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 9(\frac{1}{9})\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \operatorname{arcsec}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= \operatorname{arcsec}{\left(9 x \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

This antiderivative applies on either interval where $|9 x|>1$; the constant may differ between those intervals.

:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{5}{|x|\sqrt{7 x^{2} - 1}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Use the linear substitution $u=\sqrt{7} x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\sqrt{7},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{7})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

The substitution factor is positive, so the absolute values satisfy

$$
|u|=|\sqrt{7} x|=\sqrt{7}|x|,\qquad \frac{1}{|x|}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{|u|}.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsec}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{5}{|x|\sqrt{7 x^{2} - 1}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 5 \sqrt{7}\int \frac{1}{|\sqrt{7} x|\sqrt{(\sqrt{7} x)^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 5 \sqrt{7}(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{7})\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 5\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 5 \operatorname{arcsec}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= 5 \operatorname{arcsec}{\left(\sqrt{7} x \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

This antiderivative applies on either interval where $|\sqrt{7} x|>1$; the constant may differ between those intervals.
